topic.title: Communication-Efficient and Fault-Tolerant Distributed Training
topic.overview: Distributed training divides learning across processors, but exchanging updates and keeping models consistent can become a bottleneck. This topic studies compression, delayed aggregation, local updates, error feedback, and synchronization. Effective designs account for computation as well as communication, since reducing message size does not necessarily reduce the work needed to produce the message.
topic.whyItMatters: Wall-clock performance depends on the entire training system, including redundant gradients and hardware faults. Guarantees must connect approximate or inconsistent updates to convergence, while experiments determine whether the saved communication outweighs extra coordination and computation on actual workloads.
topic.evolution: A 2006 framework expresses many learning algorithms in a parallel map-reduce form. Later representatives compress or selectively aggregate gradients. JointSpar in 2022 avoids computing coordinates that would be discarded for transmission, and 2026 work studies silent aggregation errors, using dynamic synchronization to limit the resulting divergence between distributed model copies.
openQuestions: When should a system spend extra local computation to avoid communication?
How can synchronization distinguish harmless compression error from persistent hardware corruption?

papers.title: Sketching for Distributed Deep Learning: A Sharper Analysis
papers.tldr: A Hessian-based analysis gives dimension-independent convergence and communication guarantees for sketch-based distributed learning.

papers.title: SLowcalSGD : Slow Query Points Improve Local-SGD for Stochastic Convex Optimization
papers.tldr: SLowcalSGD uses slow query points to reduce local-update bias and provably improve on two distributed SGD baselines in heterogeneous convex optimization.

papers.title: ATA: Adaptive Task Allocation for Efficient Resource Management in Distributed Machine Learning
papers.tldr: ATA learns how to allocate distributed training tasks efficiently when worker computation times are heterogeneous and initially unknown.

papers.title: Beyond Communication Overhead: A Multilevel Monte Carlo Approach for Mitigating Compression Bias in Distributed Learning
papers.tldr: A Multilevel Monte Carlo scheme turns biased gradient compressors into statistically unbiased estimators for distributed learning.

papers.title: Distributed Parallel Gradient Stacking(DPGS): Solving Whole Slide Image Stacking Challenge in Multi-Instance Learning
papers.tldr: DPGS combines lossless multiple-instance data stacking with model-gradient compression to accelerate whole slide image training and improve accuracy.

papers.title: Distributed Retraction-Free and Communication-Efficient Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold
papers.tldr: EF-Landing reduces communication in distributed Stiefel-manifold optimization while avoiding retractions and preserving established asymptotic convergence speedups.

papers.title: Efficient Distributed Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise
papers.tldr: TailOPT uses adaptive optimization and clipping to make distributed training efficient and provably convergent under heavy-tailed gradient noise.

papers.title: Occult: Optimizing Collaborative Communications across Experts for Accelerated Parallel MoE Training and Inference
papers.tldr: Occult reduces communication among co-activated experts, reporting over 50% speedups across multiple MoE tasks and models.

papers.title: Ringmaster ASGD: The First Asynchronous SGD with Optimal Time Complexity
papers.tldr: Ringmaster ASGD achieves theoretically optimal time complexity despite arbitrary differences and fluctuations in worker computation times.

papers.title: ACCO: Accumulate While You Communicate for Communication-Overlapped Sharded LLM Training
papers.tldr: ACCO overlaps delayed-gradient synchronization with new computation to accelerate sharded LLM training while addressing the optimization effects of delayed updates.

papers.title: Approximate Gradient Coding for Distributed Learning with Heterogeneous Stragglers
papers.tldr: A gradient-coding scheme accounts for unequal worker straggler probabilities to reduce estimation error and accelerate distributed learning.

papers.title: DUO: No Compromise to Accuracy Degradation
papers.tldr: DUO overlaps high-precision gradient synchronization with computation to recover accuracy lost through aggressive gradient compression.

papers.title: Sketched Adaptive Distributed Deep Learning: A Sharp Convergence Analysis
papers.tldr: SADL combines gradient sketching with adaptive optimization and supplies high-probability convergence guarantees with only logarithmic dependence on parameter count.

papers.title: Understanding Outer Optimizers in Local SGD: Learning Rates, Momentum, and Acceleration
papers.tldr: The paper shows how Local SGD's outer learning rate balances error and noise, compensates for inner-rate mistuning, and can sometimes exceed one.

papers.title: Identifying and Mitigating Errors in Gradient Aggregation of Distributed Data Parallel Training
papers.tldr: PAFT counters silent gradient-aggregation errors through parameter synchronization scheduled to limit divergence and training overhead.

papers.title: LoRDO: Distributed Low-Rank Optimization with Infrequent Communication
papers.tldr: LoRDO combines low-rank optimization with infrequent synchronization, achieving near-parity with low-rank DDP while reducing communication by about tenfold.
